D: A desk-bound CIA analyst goes undercover across Europe to stop an arms deal.
P: Serve the snacks when Susan goes into the field.
S: Cat lady cover croque monsieur bites
Susan's first cover, the frumpy cat lady

Ham and gruyère toasties smothered in nutmeg béchamel and grilled until bubbling, cut into fingers and served with cornichons and Dijon. Melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp plain flour for 1 minute, then whisk in 200ml milk and simmer until thick. Season with nutmeg and stir in 40g grated gruyère. Spread 8 slices of white bread thinly with Dijon mustard. Make 4 sandwiches with 150g sliced leg ham and 80g gruyère. Fry in butter for 2 minutes a side, then spread the béchamel on top, scatter with 40g more gruyère and grill 3 minutes until bubbling. Cut into fingers.
Budapest garlic lángos with sour cream
the Budapest leg of the mission

Hungarian fried flatbread brushed with garlic oil, topped with cool sour cream, grated cheese and a sprinkle of paprika and dill. Divide 500g pizza dough into 4 balls and rest 15 minutes. Stretch each by hand into a 15cm round, thinner in the middle. Fry in 3cm of oil at 180C for 90 seconds a side until puffed and golden, then drain. Mix 2 crushed garlic cloves with 3 tbsp olive oil and brush over the hot bread. Spread each with 3 tbsp sour cream, scatter with 120g grated tasty cheese and finish with sweet paprika and chopped dill.
M: Rome cacio e pepe with toasted pepper

Spaghetti tossed in a glossy sauce of pecorino, toasted cracked black pepper and starchy pasta water, finished with extra cheese at the table. Cook 400g spaghetti in well-salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Meanwhile toast 2 tsp coarsely cracked black pepper in a large dry frying pan for 1 minute, then add 30g butter and a ladle of the pasta water. Finely grate 150g pecorino and mix to a paste with 4 tbsp cool pasta water. Move the pasta into the pepper pan with a splash more water and toss 1 minute. Off the heat, toss in the cheese paste until glossy and serve with extra pecorino.
W: A moist chocolate sheet cake with thick fudge icing and chopped toasted hazelnuts, cut into big squares for the office crowd. Mix 300g self-raising flour, 300g caster sugar, 60g cocoa and 1 tsp bicarb. Whisk in 2 eggs, 250ml milk, 125ml vegetable oil and 250ml hot coffee to a thin batter. Pour into a lined 23 x 33cm tin and bake at 180C for 30 minutes. Cool. For the icing, melt 100g butter and 150g dark chocolate, then beat in 250g icing sugar and 3 tbsp milk. Spread over the cake and scatter with 60g chopped toasted hazelnuts.
K: Rayna and her very big hair in Rome

A bitter orange aperitif topped with prosecco and soda over ice, with a fat wedge of blood orange and a green olive on the side. Fill 4 large wine glasses with ice. Pour 60ml bitter orange aperitif into each, then add 90ml chilled prosecco and 30ml soda water. Stir gently once. Slide a thick wedge of blood orange, or regular orange, into each glass and serve with a small bowl of green olives on the side. For anyone not drinking, mix blood orange juice with soda and a dash of bitters.

dishes.n: Cat lady cover croque monsieur bites

steps.text: Melt some of the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk and simmer until thick. Season with nutmeg and stir in a little gruyere.
Spread the bread thinly with Dijon and make sandwiches with ham and gruyere.
Fry the sandwiches in butter on both sides.
Spread the bechamel on top, scatter with more gruyere and grill until bubbling.
Cut into fingers and serve with cornichons.

dishes.n: Budapest garlic lángos with sour cream

steps.text: Divide the dough into four balls and rest.
Stretch each by hand into a round, thinner in the middle.
Fry in about 3cm of oil at 180C, turning once, until puffed and golden. Drain.
Mix the garlic with the olive oil and brush over the hot bread.
Spread with sour cream, scatter with cheese, paprika and dill.

dishes.n: Rome cacio e pepe with toasted pepper

ingredients.item: pecorino, finely grated, plus extra to serve

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says.
Toast the pepper in a large dry frying pan, then add the butter and a ladle of pasta water.
Mix most of the pecorino to a paste with cool pasta water.
Move the pasta into the pepper pan with a splash more water and toss. Off the heat, toss in the cheese paste until glossy. Serve with extra pecorino.
Mix the flour, sugar, cocoa and bicarb. Whisk in the eggs, most of the milk, oil and hot coffee to a thin batter.
Pour into a lined 23 x 33cm tin and bake at 180C.
Cool the cake.
Melt the butter and chocolate, then beat in the icing sugar and remaining milk.
Spread the icing over the cake and scatter with hazelnuts.
Fill large wine glasses with ice.
Pour the aperitif into each, then add the prosecco and soda water. Stir gently once.
Slide a thick wedge of blood orange into each glass and serve with a bowl of olives.
